title: The Collatz map, live
intro: **Code items run.** Each one is Python, run on one interpreter for the whole board, in reading order (the small numbers), and reactively, as a notebook's cells are: change `start` (in Edit, double-click it, then Shift+Enter) and what reads it runs again. Any note can have code, and **{ }** on an item hides or shows its code. Use **→** for the tour.

nodes.title: The Collatz map
nodes.text: Halve an even number; send an odd $n$ to $3n + 1$. Every start tried so far reaches $1$ (the conjecture, open since 1937).

nodes.title: The orbit
Its path
nodes.code:
path = collatz(start)
print(len(path) - 1, "steps, as high as", max(path))

nodes.title: Longest below 1000
nodes.code:
best = max(range(1, 1000), key=lambda k: len(collatz(k)))
print(best, "takes", len(collatz(best)) - 1, "steps")

steps.say: A function, defined in a code item: the items after it in reading order can call it.
`path` reads `start` and calls `collatz`. Change `start` to $97$ and this item, and the one below it, run again.
Output shows under the code, and the board makes room for it.
Items that do not read `start` do not rerun when it changes.
